title: Supreme Court Rejects Colorado Law Banning ‘Conversion Therapy’ for L.G.B.T.Q. Minors
partialText: The state and more than 20 others restrict therapists from trying to change the gender identity or sexual orientation of L.G.B.T.Q. clients under the age of 18.

title: Trump Faces a Decision on Whether to Start a Ground War in Iran
partialText: The president wants a negotiation, but the Iranians say they are refusing until a cease-fire is declared. And while Marines and the 82nd Airborne Division offer new leverage, the risks escalate quickly.

title: Europe Has a ‘Guns vs. Butter’ Problem. War in Iran Makes It Worse.
partialText: After decades of prioritizing domestic over military spending, the continent’s leaders are trying to pivot. That is straining national budgets and could anger voters.

title: U.S. Gas Prices Hit $4 a Gallon on Average, a ‘Headache’ for Drivers and Trump
partialText: A month since the first U.S.-Israeli attacks and Iran’s response effectively shut off Persian Gulf oil, drivers are paying significantly more to fill up.

title: Drivers Count Their Pennies as Gas Hits $4 a Gallon Because of War in Iran
partialText: Since the Iran conflict began on Feb. 28, gas prices across the United States have increased about 35 percent. They are now above $4 a gallon, and drivers are wincing.

title: Will $4 Gas Hurt Trump’s Approval Ratings? Here’s What History Shows.
partialText: Presidents since at least the Carter administration have seen their approval ratings tied to gas prices. But there are signs the correlation may be weakening.

title: Pentagon Weighs Using Anti-Drone Lasers Near D.C. Military Base
partialText: Sightings of drones around Fort McNair, the Army base where Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio live, have prompted consideration of deploying the new technology.

title: ‘The Book of Mormon’ Is Sorry if You Were Offended for 15 Years
partialText: The taboo-busting, gasp-inducing Broadway musical comedy has been a hit with audiences and critics. But could it be produced today?

title: ‘God Squad’ Waives Environmental Rules for Drilling in the Gulf of Mexico
partialText: The panel voted to override Endangered Species Act restrictions on oil and gas activities in the Gulf of Mexico, home to critically endangered whales and other imperiled wildlife.

title: Trump Posts Video of Presidential Library in Miami
partialText: President Trump posted a video rendering that appeared to include elements generated by artificial intelligence of a skyscraper in Miami featuring what appeared to be Air Force One.

title: New Book by JD Vance Will Explore His Conversion to Catholicism
partialText: The vice president’s book, to be released in June, will detail his return to Christianity after leaving the loosely evangelical practice of his childhood.

title: A New Jersey Teen Finds Treasure, and More, in Abandoned Storage Units
partialText: Michael Haskell, 17, set out to make some money from his locker dives. He ended up learning about life.

title: Putin’s Internet Blackout: A Chaotic Drive to Cut Off Russians From the World
partialText: With new outages and blockages, President Vladimir V. Putin is taking his boldest steps yet to control Russians’ communications.

title: Inside Russia During an Internet Crackdown
partialText: Our international correspondent Valerie Hopkins walks us through how she connects to the internet in Russia as the Kremlin clamps down and Moscow experiences major internet blackouts.

title: A Cat-and-Mouse Game of Russian Internet Restrictions and Evasion
partialText: As the Kremlin spends heavily on censorship technology, Russians are scrambling to find new ways to circumvent the limits.

title: Cesar Chavez Was a Voice for Mexican Americans Like Me. Now, We Grieve.
partialText: The United Farm Workers co-founder had been celebrated as an exemplar of civil rights. Then, a Times investigation found extensive evidence of his abuse of women.

title: On What Was Once Chavez Day, Some Try to Highlight a Movement, Not a Man
partialText: The reconsideration of the legacy of Cesar Chavez after he was accused of abusing women and girls has led some to question the lionization of icons, when reality is so often a letdown.

title: How Cesar Chavez Abused His Power
partialText: The civil rights icon had a history of sexually abusing women and girls, which the Times reporters Manny Fernandez and Sarah Hurtes spent five years investigating. They spoke to “The Daily” about how they uncovered the story.

title: In a Moment of Division, the Astronauts on the Artemis II Mission Hope to Inspire
partialText: Can the four astronauts of the NASA mission Artemis II make a difference in a distracted and divided world?

title: For Trump, the Artemis II Moon Mission Offers a Shot to Cement His Legacy
partialText: No president since the Apollo era has pushed harder to return to the moon than President Trump. But he wants a space achievement that is about “more than getting rocks this time.”

title: First Canadian Astronaut Will Travel to the Moon Amid Fraying U.S.-Canada Relations
partialText: Canada will send its first astronaut to the moon on a joint mission with the United States, but back on Earth, the relationship between the two countries is fraying.

title: How the Internet Became the ‘Cookbook’ of the Drug Trade
partialText: A baffling overdose death took investigators to the frontier of ultra-potent synthetic drugs. The clues were hauntingly familiar.

title: McCormick to Combine With Unilever Food Unit to Create a Spice Giant
partialText: The deal ends Unilever’s time in the food industry and will create a multibillion-dollar group under the McCormick name.

title: Eli Lilly Will Buy a Narcolepsy Drug Developer for $6.3 Billion
partialText: Eli Lilly plans to acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals, which has been conducting a midstage clinical trial of its lead drug.

title: The People Trump Pardoned Are on a Crime Spree
partialText: The president and the Republican Party deserve to pay a political price for the pardons.

title: It’s Not Going to Get Any Easier for Democrats After Trump
partialText: The party will come up against a demographic cliff in 2032.

title: A Lifeline for Cuba
partialText: We look at the energy crisis on the Caribbean island.

title: Don’t Know Where to Go This Summer? Let Us Help!
partialText: We’re responding to readers’ travel quandaries with our suggestions.

title: FDA Is Expected to Lift Restriction on Peptides, Heeding RFK Jr.’s Wishes
partialText: The peptides, which are increasingly marketed as providing longevity and health benefits, were removed in 2023 from the agency’s list of products that compounding pharmacies can sell.

title: The Push to Ban Cars From All New York City Parks
partialText: Central Park is car-free, and so is Prospect Park. What about the rest?
